key_insight: Tetris3D improves single-image 3D scene reconstruction by generating objects that physically and geometrically fit together, rather than placing each object in isolation. The key idea is to condition each object on its neighbors so the reconstructed scene is more coherent and realistic.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of fine-grained spatial compatibility in 3D scene generation from a single image. Existing methods often fail to enforce how neighboring objects should align, interact, or fit together in a physically plausible way.
method: Generates 3D scene objects with explicit conditioning on surrounding object geometry.
Encourages local spatial compatibility so adjacent objects better match in shape, placement, and interaction.
Reconstructs a complete scene from one image while aiming for physical and geometric coherence.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it can produce more realistic 3D reconstructions that are better suited for downstream tasks like robotics, AR/VR, and scene editing. It also shows a practical direction for improving generative models by incorporating local geometric constraints.

paper_title: Tetris3D: 3D Scene Generation With Objects That Fit Together
paper_authors: Jaeyeong Kim, Jinhyuk Jang, Jongmin Lee, Kyehong Park, Seungryong Kim
